title: This is the hardest thing I have ever seen - Howard Marks on the AI Frenzy
summary: In this episode, Howard Marks — co-chairman of Oaktree Capital and one of the most careful thinkers on risk in the business — works through the question everyone is circling: are markets excessively e We look at where today's valuations sit against the historical record — what buying into elevated multiples has meant for returns over the following decade, and why the answer has been remarkably cons Marks's answer is about posture — where you sit on the aggressive-to-defensive dial, what you're being paid to take risk, and the discipline of calibration over prediction.

reader_summary.headline: Howard Marks discusses whether the AI market frenzy is a bubble or just high optimism.
reader_summary.overview: Howard Marks explains that a bubble is a mindset where investors believe any price is acceptable, not just a specific price level. He notes that technology can be valuable even if the stock price is too high. The episode explores historical data showing that high prices lead to lower future returns rather than predicting crashes.

key_points.text: A bubble is a state of mind where investors stop asking if an asset is worth its cost.
key_points.evidence_quote: A bubble isn't a price level; it's a state of mind. It's what happens when investors stop asking whether an asset is worth what it costs and start believing that no price is too high.

key_points.text: High prices do not predict crashes, but they do predict lower returns for the future.
key_points.evidence_quote: High prices don't predict crashes. They predict lower future returns.

key_points.text: Investors should focus on their risk posture and discipline instead of trying to time the market top.

reader_summary.why_it_matters: Listeners learn to distinguish between a great company and a good investment while avoiding the trap of trying to predict market tops.
